narrative_purpose: Give the reader the transferable skill of the chapter: four wing planforms side by side, each shape visibly answering a different question about how to live in air.
subject: Four wing silhouettes arranged in a single row against darkness, all at the same scale, each shown as a pale flat plan-view shape. FIRST from left: one extremely long, narrow, straight wing pair - the ocean soarer. SECOND: a short, broad, rounded wing pair with a blunt tip. THIRD: a swept-back sharply pointed wing pair. FOURTH: a compact arrangement of TWO short paired wings, one set behind the other, occupying the same total area as the others but in half the width.
scene: An abstract dark field, the four silhouettes floating in a row with even spacing, nothing else in frame.
camera: Flat plan view from directly above, all four specimens at identical scale and on one level baseline.
light: Each silhouette faintly self-luminous along its leading edge - the first three in cool cyan, the fourth in warmer teal so the odd one out reads as different.
palette: Deep indigo void, pale grey-white wing forms, cyan edge glow on the first three, teal on the fourth.
style: Painterly museum specimen sheet, brushed and hand-worked, like pressed wings pinned on dark board.
detail_level: Crisp clean outlines on all four, faint membrane texture within each, plain void between them.
composition: Four forms in an evenly spaced horizontal row, all sharing one baseline, generous plain dark space above each framed by deep negative space.
consistency_notes: Wings only - no bodies, heads or feet, so the reader compares planform and nothing else. All four at the same scale and same total area, differing only in shape and proportion. The fourth must clearly be TWO pairs in tandem, visibly narrower in span than the other three.
negative_prompt: no text, no lettering, no numbers, no labels, no arrows, no rulers or scale bars, no vector-flat infographic look, no photographic or 3D render, no cartoon style, no bird heads or bodies
